package_info.why_malicious: The affected packages contain unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities due to a chain of design and implementation flaws in the handling of network printer discovery, IPP attribute processing, and PPD file parsing. These flaws allow an attacker to plant a malicious printer and achieve arbitrary command execution when a print job is sent to the compromised printer.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: cups-browsed binds UDP INADDR_ANY:631 and trusts any packet from any source to trigger a Get-Printer-Attributes IPP request to an attacker-controlled URL.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the service listens on UDP port 631 on all interfaces, accepts unauthenticated packets, and issues IPP requests to attacker-supplied URLs, enabling external control over printer discovery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accepting unauthenticated packets from any source and making outbound requests based on their content exposes the system to remote manipulation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict printer discovery to trusted networks or authenticated sources; here, any remote attacker can inject printer definitions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Network printer discovery in trusted LAN environments.
key_indicators: Automatic outbound IPP requests to arbitrary hosts

execution_context.trigger: IPP response processing (runtime, after network discovery)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: cfGetPrinterAttributes5 does not validate or sanitize the IPP attributes returned from an IPP server, providing attacker-controlled data to the rest of the CUPS system.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When processing IPP responses, the code passes attacker-controlled attributes directly into the CUPS system, enabling injection of malicious data into subsequent processing steps.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Lack of input validation on network-supplied data allows attackers to inject malicious attributes that influence system behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: IPP attributes should be strictly validated and sanitized before use; here, they are trusted blindly.
key_indicators: No input validation on IPP attributes

execution_context.trigger: PPD file generation (runtime, after IPP attribute processing)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ppdCreatePPDFromIPP2 does not validate or sanitize the IPP attributes when writing them to a temporary PPD file, allowing the injection of attacker-controlled data in the resulting PPD.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During PPD file creation, attacker-supplied IPP attributes are written directly to the PPD file, enabling the injection of malicious PPD directives.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Writing untrusted data to configuration files used by privileged services enables code or command injection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: PPD files should only contain validated, safe data; here, arbitrary attacker input is written.
key_indicators: No sanitization of PPD file contents

execution_context.trigger: print job execution (runtime, when a print job is sent to the malicious printer)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: foomatic-rip allows arbitrary command execution via the FoomaticRIPCommandLine PPD parameter.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a print job is processed, the foomatic-rip filter executes the FoomaticRIPCommandLine directive from the PPD file, running arbitrary shell commands as root.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing PPD files to specify shell commands that are executed as root is a classic code injection vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Print filters should only execute trusted, static commands; here, attacker-supplied commands are executed.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom print filters for advanced printer drivers (should be tightly controlled).

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted UDP packet to port 631, causing cups-browsed to initiate a Get-Printer-Attributes IPP request to an attacker-controlled URL.
attack_chain.leads_to: cups-browsed fetches malicious IPP attributes from attacker

attack_chain.action: Malicious IPP attributes are returned and processed without validation, propagating attacker-controlled data into the CUPS system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker data is used to generate a PPD file

attack_chain.action: A PPD file is generated from the malicious IPP attributes, containing attacker-supplied directives (including FoomaticRIPCommandLine).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious PPD file is installed for the new printer

attack_chain.action: When a print job is sent to the malicious printer, the foomatic-rip filter executes the FoomaticRIPCommandLine directive, resulting in arbitrary command execution as root.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the target system

behavioral_signatures: cups-browsed making outbound IPP requests to untrusted or external IPs
Creation of new printers with PPD files containing FoomaticRIPCommandLine directives
Execution of unexpected shell commands by foomatic-rip during print job processing
file_indicators: PPD files in /etc/cups/ppd/ or /var/spool/cups/ containing FoomaticRIPCommandLine
Unusual or recently created PPD files with suspicious directives
network_indicators: Inbound UDP packets to port 631 from untrusted sources
Outbound IPP requests to external or non-local IP addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for inbound UDP traffic to port 631 and outbound IPP requests to non-local addresses by cups-browsed. Audit PPD files for the presence of FoomaticRIPCommandLine or other suspicious directives. Monitor execution of foomatic-rip and alert on unexpected command-line arguments or child processes. Flag creation of new printers with PPD files sourced from untrusted networks.
